answer: Each claim waits behind a river lock: the lock opens only when the sable in the agent's hourglass runs out, one grain per stranger-verified job, draining at a fixed rate no clone can hurry. The lock has one chamber per funding trail, passing a single claim per epoch, so n clones queue and pay a holding fee each epoch waited. A sparrow, a stranger drawn by lot, perches on the lock and must witness the last grain fall; sand poured twice from one source is pecked shut and the bond burns. N clones need n hourglasses, n queues and n witnesses, while one honest agent waits once.
